summary:
FLAME WATCH is an interactive simulation and Synthetic Intelligence (SI) platform developed to address fire safety risks in microgravity environments aboard spacecraft and to democratize training in this field.

In space, the absence of gravity and buoyancy means that flames do not rise upward as they do on Earth; instead, they take on a spherical shape, smoke remains suspended in the air, and "cool flames"—invisible to the naked eye—can persist undetected for weeks, posing a critical danger. To overcome the limitations of traditional static reports in conveying these complex physical phenomena, we have developed a five-layered architecture based on actual flight data from NASA’s PSI and NTRS programs (including BASS, Saffire, FLEX, and SAME). The platform features a six-stage mission-based game that explores historical crises—such as those involving Apollo 1 and the Mir space station—a real-time physics simulator for testing parameters like gravity and oxygen levels, a data laboratory for comparing flight data, and an evidence-based safety assistant designed to operate without "hallucinations."

Crew safety is paramount during long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars, such as those planned under the Artemis program. By transforming raw scientific data into an interactive decision-support and training tool, FLAME WATCH aims to anticipate and prevent fire-related risks in future space exploration.
details:
FLAME WATCH is an interactive microgravity fire safety simulation and Synthetic Intelligence (SI) platform built on real NASA PSI and NTRS flight datasets (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, and SAME).

How It Works and Key Features: In microgravity (g = 0), flames form pale blue spheres, soot remains suspended, and invisible cool flames can linger undetected. Our 5-layer architecture translates these physics into an accessible tool:

  • Guided Mission Game: A 6-stage scenario game solving historical crises (Apollo 1, Mir 1997) and designing a fire-safe Lunar base.
  • Live Flame Physics Simulator: Real-time visualization adjusting gravity (0g to 1g), oxygen (15% to 100%), pressure, and airflow.
  • NASA Data Lab: Filter and compare over 20 NASA flight tests side-by-side.
  • Synthetic Intelligence (SI) Assistant: An offline, rule-based safety assistant citing verified NTRS and PSI papers with zero hallucination risk.
  • Research Horizon: Models partial-gravity fire risks on the Moon (0.16g) and Mars (0.38g) for Artemis missions.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

  • Accessibility: Transforms dense technical reports into intuitive visual simulations for students, researchers, and engineers.
  • Reliability: Guarantees 100% evidence-based, offline-capable decision support critical for long-duration Artemis space missions.

Tech Stack:

  • Frontend and Physics Engine: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), and HTML5 Canvas for real-time flame morphology rendering.
  • Data and SI Core: Structured JSON matrices derived from NASA PSI and NTRS datasets paired with a deterministic rule-based matching engine.
  • Deployment: Hosted via GitHub and Vercel for instant global access.

Creativity and Team Considerations:

  • Creativity: Bridges the gap between rigid academic PDFs and gamified simulation, replacing error-prone generative AI with a strictly verified Synthetic Intelligence approach.
  • Key Factors: Strict adherence to experimental physics (such as airflow-induced flame spread and partial-gravity flammability spikes) alongside zero-dependency, client-side performance.
